title: Advanced Excel Automation & Analysis
preferred_referent: 📍 External Advanced Excel Automation & Analysis specification
boundary: Create a repeatable native-Excel/VBA one-click workflow that cleans same-structure raw files, removes duplicates, handles missing regression rows, normalizes formatting, runs a regression, outputs coefficients/R²/residuals, and rebuilds a dashboard with a residual plot.
acceptance: One macro-enabled .xlsm containing all cleaning/regression procedures; automatically refreshed dashboard; end-to-end execution under 30 seconds on about 20,000 rows; and successful tests on client unseen datasets.
result: PROTOTYPE PASS — demo replay cleaned 245 raw rows to 233 usable rows, removed 5 duplicates and 7 incomplete regression rows, and independently reconciled R² 0.98953813 with coefficients 1.763978803 (MarketingSpend) and 0.812960824 (Visits). Final VBA execution/runtime and unseen-dataset acceptance remain pending.
next_movement: In desktop Microsoft Excel, import RegressionAutomation.bas into the demo workbook, save as .xlsm, run the 20,000-row benchmark fixture, verify elapsed time under 30 seconds, inspect the residual/dashboard output, then test against client unseen datasets when supplied.
blockers: This environment does not execute desktop Excel VBA.
Final .xlsm packaging requires desktop Excel macro import/save.
The under-30-second criterion has not been measured in Excel.
Client unseen datasets are not publicly supplied.
resume_bullets: Designed a native Excel/VBA cleaning and multiple-regression pipeline around a bounded external specification.
Built a settings-driven demo dashboard with coefficients, R-squared, predicted values, residuals, and a residual chart.
Created a 20,000-row benchmark fixture and an independent regression oracle while preserving unverified VBA/runtime criteria as explicit blockers.
notes: The workbook is a visual/demo shell; RegressionAutomation.bas must be imported in desktop Excel and saved as .xlsm before final delivery.
Do not claim the client 20k-row runtime criterion or unseen-dataset criterion as passed until actually measured.
